title: AFIR and ISO 15118-20: what changes on 1 January 2027 | VOOL
description: From 1 January 2027 newly installed AC charging points in the EU must support ISO 15118-20. The new VOOL Charger does, and existing VOOL chargers can be upgraded.

sections.title: Chargers installed from 1 January 2027 need ISO 15118-20. VOOL is ready.
sections.lead: The new VOOL Charger supports ISO 15118-2, ISO 15118-20 and Plug & Charge. It ships from mid-December 2026. Chargers you already have can be upgraded.

sections.title: What the rules say
points: Since 8 January 2026: newly installed or renovated publicly accessible AC charging points must support EN ISO 15118-2.
From 1 January 2027: newly installed or renovated AC (Mode 3) charging points must support EN ISO 15118-20. This covers public and private charging points.
Existing chargers stay as they are. The rule applies to new installations and renovations, not to chargers installed before the deadline.
Public charging points must also offer ad hoc payment without a contract and show the price before charging starts. For AC, a QR code payment page is enough.
paragraphs: The rules come from the EU’s Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) and its delegated regulation (EU) 2025/656. The Commission is still publishing guidance on the details, so check the current text before a tender.

items.title: ISO 15118-2 and -20
items.text: Both versions from the first day, so the charger meets the 2026 and the 2027 requirements.

items.title: Plug & Charge
items.text: The car identifies itself when it is plugged in. No app or card needed to start.

items.title: V2G later, without new hardware
items.text: Bidirectional charging arrives as a firmware update in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: Same charger otherwise
items.text: Up to 22 kW, 6.5 m cable, load management with VOOL LMC and a 5-year warranty.

items.title: Available from mid-December 2026
items.text: Production has switched to the ISO 15118 charger. Ask your reseller about delivery dates.

items.title: Developed in-house
items.text: The ISO 15118 software is VOOL’s own, built by the team that makes the charger.

sections.alt: The orange VOOL charge controller inside the charger casing
sections.title: Already have VOOL chargers? Upgrade the controller.
sections.text: Current VOOL chargers do not support ISO 15118, and they do not have to: they were installed before the deadline. If you want Plug & Charge or V2G, the charge controller can be swapped for the new one. The casing, cabling and cable stay.
points: The swap takes a few minutes and the tool ships with the controller
Price will be announced in December 2026

items.title: VOOL Commercial Pole
items.text: Two 22 kW charging points with a display, QR code payment and an optional MID meter.

items.title: Billing and payments
items.text: Ad hoc payment, pricing and payouts are handled by the VOOL platform.

items.q: Can I still install the current VOOL charger in December 2026?
items.a: Yes. The ISO 15118-20 requirement applies to charging points installed or renovated from 1 January 2027.

items.q: Do I have to replace chargers that are already installed?
items.a: No. Chargers installed before the deadline can stay. An upgrade is your choice.

items.q: Does the rule apply to a private home?
items.a: From 1 January 2027 it covers newly installed private AC charging points too.
The car and the charger identify each other over the charging cable, so charging and billing start without an app or a card.
The new charger gets bidirectional charging by firmware update in the first quarter of 2027. Your car and your grid operator’s rules also have to allow it.

sections.title: Planning installations for 2027?
sections.lead: Tell us what you are building. We will confirm what you need to comply.
